about: My Back is a frame of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker grimacing next to a parked car, face scrunched in pain, with the subtitle "My back." printed underneath. The joke is that a superhero, in his twenties, sounds exactly like a middle-aged dad after a minor effort. It's used for any small activity that leaves you feeling unexpectedly old, from getting off the floor to sleeping in a slightly wrong position.
origin: The scene is from Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2 (2004). Peter, whose powers are failing, tries to swing between rooftops, plunges into an alley and gets up muttering about his back. It became a popular template in the early 2020s.
usage:
This template has one text box at the top. Write the trigger, the everyday thing that broke you, and let the built-in subtitle "My back." deliver the punchline. Don't repeat "my back" in your caption.

Good triggers are tiny physical efforts that shouldn't hurt: sneezing, standing up after a long meeting, picking up a sock, playing with your kids for five minutes, or sleeping on a new pillow. It's even better for gamers and office workers who sit all day.
ideas: bending down to pick up the TV remote
me after one game of pickup basketball
waking up from a nap on the couch
carrying all the grocery bags in one trip
